caseno: Civil Appeal No. 108 of 1977 from Civil Rule No. 419 of 1974.
lawyer:
Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed. Advocate, instructed by A Rob II, Advocate-on-Record -----For the Appellants. 
Abdus Salam, Senior Advocate, instructed by B.C. Pandey, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Abdus Sattar & ors ----- Appellants.
Vs.
Suresh Chandra Das & ors ----- Respondents.
full_judgment: 6. Since the question will not take as long, we propose to deal with it first. It is now well settled that a revision under section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act lies if there is an error of law involved in the decision or the trial Court. A revision is available with a wider scope than that under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. They are now well settled and require no further elaboration. What is to be seen is whether the learned Judge of the High Court provision has applied the correct principle in interfering with the decision of the trial Court under section 25 of the said Act. First of all, he is to come to a finding the decision of the Court below suffers from an error of law, and then to see whether the error of law has vitiated its decision, and on so finding, he can proceed to reverse the decision of the trial Court. Keeping this principle in view, we are to judge the finding of the learned Single Judge regarding the reversal of the finding of the trial Court on the question of creation of tenancy in favour of Respondent 1. It is to be remembered that both the Courts below have accepted the creation of tenancy in 1968 in favour of Balaram, the father of the Respondents. Where the two Courts differed is on the creation of tenancy in favour of Respondent 1. According to the trial Court, tenancy was created in his favour in 1969 and this he based on a reference to Ext. 3 series the rent receipts. This finding was reversed by the learned Single Judge making a bare observation that it was clear from the pleadings of the parties and the evidence that the tenancy of Balaram was created on 1.1.68 and that the tenancy devolved upon his death on his heirs. The question is whether this finding is in accordance with the provisions of section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act. Plainly it is not. The learned Judge has not shown what was the error in the appreciation of evidence by the trial Court in its finding which could be termed as an error of law.which would give the High Court Division an authority under the Act to interfere. The approach of the learned Judge was as if he was dealing with a first appeal on fact and not a revision under section 25 of the said Act. No error of law was pointed out by him, nor do we find any such error in the finding of the trial Court. The trial Court from evidence drew a conclusion of fact which the learned Judge reversed without pointing out any error of law. He merely drew a second conclusion of fact which section 25 of the said Act does not authorize him to do. In this view of the matter the reversal of finding of fact by the learned Judge on this point cannot be sustained and must be set aside. The finding of the trial Court that a tenancy was created in favour of Respondent 1 on the death of Balaram, his father, must be upheld. In view of this finding, the first question loses much of its importance but since a question of law of public importance is involved, we proceed to deal with it.
